page.layout: Running head at top: page number "64" at left, title "NOTÆ." at centre. Main text in one column on the right. Left margin holds two notes: a starred note at the level of "Fuisse illi" and an italic note "Abul Feda." beside the following lines. Three numbered entries (47, 48, 49) at the foot of the column.

main_text.p: tes. Abraham sc. istum Tamani sub أصحمة[?] Asʿhama Alnajashi, seu Æthiopum rege, præfectum in urbe Sanaa Ecclesiam struxisse, ad quem, neglectui habitâ Caabâ, peregrinationes ab hominibus institui voluit. eam cùm Arabs quidam conspurcâssent, & indignè tractâssent ad iram provocatum Abraham sc ad diruendam Caabam juramento obstrinxisse, atque ejus rei gratiâ collectis copiis Meccham rectâ retendisse. Fuisse illi {*}Elephantem nomine محمود[?] Mahmud, qui cum jam Meccæ propinquus faciem Caabæ advertere cogeretur in genua procumbens progredi recusabat; cùm alio alacriter pergebat. Misisse autem Deum avium greges quæ singulæ ternos gestabant lapillos, ore unum, pedibus reliquos, magnitudine inter lenticulam & cicerem, ejus tamen ponderis, ut cùm in hominem galeâ obtectum decidèrent, perforatis galeâ & homine (addunt Jallalani, & Elephanto) in terram caderent. iis inscripta fuisse perdendorum nomina. Vide AlCeshaph[?], AlBidawium, Jallalani, qui Commentarios in Alc. scripserunt: & historicos Abul Fedam, AlJannabium, Ahmedem, &c. contigisse hoc tradunt anno Anusherwani 42, quo & natus est Mohammedes.ut alii, (teste Abul Feda) plu-rēt[?].Abul Feda.
main_text.l: 48 مسروق[?] Masruk, Abrahæ filius, qui ultimus Æthiopum Tamano imperavit, reverso ad Hamyarensis regno. Æthiopum autem imperium annos 72. circiter durâsse refert Allannabius; regnante Aryato, 20. Abrahah, 50 circiter. Tacsumo, duos.
49 سيف بن ذي يزن[?] Saif Ebn Di Yazan, Hamyarensis, [?] qui imperavit ab Anusherwano rege Persarum, (quas frustra prius ab Heraclio Imperatore petierat)

page.notes: Arabic words are transcribed from the scan and marked [?] where the letters are not clearly legible. "Ceshaph" in "AlCeshaph" and the reading of the star note's last word ("plu-rēt") are doubtful. In entry 49 the comma after "Hamyarensis" and the word "qui" are partly obscured by a stain. The "Abul Feda." note is placed beside the lines it appears to accompany; its exact position is approximate. The scan is cut off at the right edge of the column, so the last word of entry 49 may be incomplete.
